title: Annotatio IV §.XXII open: Reformeds’ dual exposition of spiritual presence — in the body itself vs in the mode
pass_a_gloss: §. XXII. Meanwhile we judge it worth the labor to note that the Reformed, all to a man seriously and with whole breast believing and professing the most real presence of Christ’s body and blood in the Sacred Supper — made namely in a Spiritual mode — have yet been accustomed to expound this Spiritual presence, after the example of the Old Doctors of the Church, not simply in one and the same way, but under a certain light difference, in a Mode quite double — so indeed that some have sought and placed SPIRITUALITY here in Christ’s body and blood themselves, altogether present in the Supper; others rather in the mode of their presence.
pass_b_english: §.XXII: all the Reformed seriously confess the most real presence of Christ’s body and blood in the Supper — in a Spiritual mode.

Yet after the old Doctors they expound that spiritual presence under a light difference in a double way: some put SPIRITUALITY in the body and blood themselves present; others rather in the mode of their presence.
source_text: §. XXII. Interim annotandum operæ pretium ducimus, Reformatos realissimam corporis & sanguinis Christi in S. Cœna præsentiam, Spirituali scil. modo factam, ad unum omnes seriò totôque pectore credentes ac profitentes, Spiritualem tamen præsentiam hanc, ad exemplum Veterum Ecclesiæ Doctorum, non uno eodemque simpliciter, sed sub levi quodam discrimine, Modô admodùm duplici, exponere consuevisse, ita quidem, ut alii hîc SPIRITUALITATEM in ipso Christi corpore & sanguine, in Cœna omnino præsentibus; alii in præsentiæ horum modo potiùs, quæsiverint locaverintve.
